title: A Hausdorff module over a complete ring that is finite modulo the ideal is finite
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal and $M$ an $A$-module. Assume (1) $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]; (2) $\bigcap_{n\ge1}I^nM=0$; (3) $M/IM$ is a finitely generated $A/I$-module. Then $M$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; more precisely, any $x_1,\dots,x_r\in M$ whose images generate $M/IM$ over $A/I$ generate $M$ over $A$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031D (lemma-finite-over-complete-ring, line 22860); its proof uses Lemma Tag 0315 (lemma-completion-generalities) and Lemma Tag 031B (lemma-when-finite-module-complete-over-complete-ring, line 22843)

proof.text: Notation for all steps: $A$, $I$, $M$ satisfy (1)-(3); $x_1,\dots,x_r\in M$ are elements whose images generate $M/IM$ over $A/I$ (they exist by (3); $r=0$ is allowed), and $N=\sum_iAx_i\subseteq M$. (Generation modulo every power of $I$.) For every $k\ge0$ and every $y\in I^kM$ there are $c_1,\dots,c_r\in I^k$ with $y-\sum_ic_ix_i\in I^{k+1}M$ (with $I^0=A$). Proof: for $k=0$, the image of $y$ in $M/IM$ is $\sum_i\bar a_i\bar x_i$ with $\bar a_i\in A/I$; lifting $\bar a_i$ to $a_i\in A$ gives $y-\sum_ia_ix_i\in IM$. For $k\ge1$, write $y=\sum_jt_jm_j$ (finite sum) with $t_j\in I^k$, $m_j\in M$; by the case $k=0$, $m_j=\sum_ia_{ji}x_i+m_j'$ with $a_{ji}\in A$, $m_j'\in IM$. Then $y=\sum_ic_ix_i+\sum_jt_jm_j'$ with $c_i=\sum_jt_ja_{ji}\in I^k$ and $t_jm_j'\in I^k\cdot IM=I^{k+1}M$. (In other words $I^kM=I^kN+I^{k+1}M$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0315 (lemma-completion-generalities, line 22571), proof of (1), lines 22589-22610: the claim that K_{n+1}/I^{n+1}M -> K_n/I^nM is surjective ('write phi(x)=sum z_j n_j with z_j in I^n ... n_j = phi(m_j) + sum z_{jk} n_{jk}'), here for phi: A^r -> M

proof.text: (Successive approximation.) Fix $m\in M$. Define inductively $m_0=m$ and, for $k\ge0$ with $m_k\in I^kM$ already defined, choose by Step 1 elements $c^{(k)}_1,\dots,c^{(k)}_r\in I^k$ with $m_{k+1}:=m_k-\sum_ic^{(k)}_ix_i\in I^{k+1}M$. Put $s^{(n)}_i=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}c^{(k)}_i\in A$ for $n\ge0$. By induction on $n$ (the case $n=0$ being $m=m_0$, and $m_n=\sum_ic^{(n)}_ix_i+m_{n+1}$ giving the step), $m=\sum_is^{(n)}_ix_i+m_n$, hence $m-\sum_is^{(n)}_ix_i\in I^nM$ for every $n\ge0$. Moreover, for $n'\ge n$, $s^{(n')}_i-s^{(n)}_i=\sum_{k=n}^{n'-1}c^{(k)}_i\in I^n$, since $c^{(k)}_i\in I^k\subseteq I^n$ for $k\ge n$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0315 (lemma-completion-generalities, line 22571), proof of (1), lines 22589-22610: the claim that K_{n+1}/I^{n+1}M -> K_n/I^nM is surjective ('write phi(x)=sum z_j n_j with z_j in I^n ... n_j = phi(m_j) + sum z_{jk} n_{jk}'), here for phi: A^r -> M; the elements x' = x - sum z_j m_j of that proof are the m_{k+1} here

proof.text: (The limits of the coefficients exist in $A$.) For each $i$, the classes $(s^{(n)}_i\bmod I^n)_{n\ge1}$ form a compatible sequence, since $s^{(n+1)}_i\equiv s^{(n)}_i\pmod{I^n}$ (Step 2), i.e. an element of the completion $\varprojlim_nA/I^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. By (1) the canonical map $A\to\varprojlim_nA/I^n$, $a\mapsto(a\bmod I^n)_n$, is bijective [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]; by its surjectivity there is $a_i\in A$ with $a_i\equiv s^{(n)}_i\pmod{I^n}$ for every $n\ge1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031D (lemma-finite-over-complete-ring, line 22860), proof: 'By Lemma 0315 the map (M')^ -> M^ is surjective ... by Lemma 031B M' is complete' (lines 22874-22879); here the compatible system of 0315 lives in A^r and completeness of A (hypothesis (1)) replaces 031B and the Mittag-Leffler step of 0315

proof.text: (Conclusion.) For every $n\ge1$, $m-\sum_ia_ix_i=\bigl(m-\sum_is^{(n)}_ix_i\bigr)+\sum_i\bigl(s^{(n)}_i-a_i\bigr)x_i$, where the first summand lies in $I^nM$ by Step 2 and the second lies in $I^nM$ since $s^{(n)}_i-a_i\in I^n$ by Step 3. Hence $m-\sum_ia_ix_i\in\bigcap_{n\ge1}I^nM=0$ by (2), so $m=\sum_ia_ix_i\in N$. As $m\in M$ was arbitrary, $M=N$ is generated over $A$ by $x_1,\dots,x_r$, in particular finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031D (lemma-finite-over-complete-ring, line 22860), proof lines 22872-22885: 'the kernel of M -> M^ is zero since it is equal to the intersection of the I^nM = (0). Hence we conclude that M = M' = M^ is finitely generated'

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks 031D (algebra.tex line 22860) and kept; its 'more precisely' clause (lifts of generators of M/IM generate M) is what the Stacks proof shows. Tags 031D, 0315, 031B verified in tags/tags. Proof written in 4 elementary steps: generation modulo I^{k+1} of I^kM by the x_i with coefficients in I^k (the lifting claim in the proof of 0315 (1)); the inductive successive approximation m = sum s_i^(n) x_i + m_n with m_n in I^nM and s^(n) Cauchy; the limits a_i in A from bijectivity of A -> lim A/I^n [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; m - sum a_i x_i in the intersection of the I^nM, which is 0 by (2). This replaces the detour through completions of M' and M (0315, 031B) by the same argument carried out on A^r -> M, so no node for 0315 or 031B is needed. No new nodes. Mathlib re-searched with LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle, grep: no exact match; closest is surjective_of_mkQ_comp_surjective (Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Functoriality.lean:437), which would give the result for f: (Fin r -> A) -> M once IsPrecomplete I (Fin r -> A) is shown (no Mathlib instance). The citers lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-domain-finite-over-regular and lem-weil-pbc-finite-after-completion use the statement as written (hypotheses (1)-(3), conclusion finitely generated). lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian and lem-weil-pbc-change-ideal-completion are not needed. No Lean on master or slopmaster2.
